title: The Struggle To Commoditize AI
gist: Gavekal argues that the AI-monetization worries now hitting US AI hardware and software stocks (after Anthropic's quarterly revenue growth disappointed) surfaced earlier and more dramatically in China, where leading AI company shares have fallen substantially. China's developers run a low-margin, high-volume cheap open-weight model strategy premised on eventual commoditization, but US chip export controls cap their compute, so capacity constraints are materially limiting revenue growth.

insights.claim: Shares of AI-related hardware and software firms sold off in the week before 21 Oct 2026 after Anthropic's latest quarterly revenue growth disappointed some market participants, signalling rising investor worry about how leading US AI model developers will make money.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Model-developer revenue prints have become a sector-wide sentiment driver for the AI hardware/software complex, not just a private-company datapoint.
insights.locator: The jitters in global equity markets

insights.claim: Monetization worries about AI surfaced earlier and more dramatically in China than in the US, with China's leading AI companies seeing their share prices decline substantially in recent months.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: China's AI equity drawdown can be read as a leading indicator of what a monetization scare looks like when usage growth fails to convert to revenue.
insights.quote: those same worries about monetization surfaced much earlier—and in a more dramatic way—in China
insights.locator: The jitters in global equity markets

insights.claim: Although China's open-weight AI models have surged in popularity, Chinese AI companies are struggling to translate that usage into revenue growth.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Adoption metrics for open-weight models are a poor proxy for developer revenue; investors should value on monetized usage, not downloads or popularity.
insights.quote: while China’s open-weight models have surged in popularity, the companies are struggling to translate that usage into revenue growth

insights.claim: China's AI developers deliberately pursue a low-margin, high-volume business of offering cheap models to a vast number of users, partly because they expect the entire AI industry to eventually become commoditized.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A volume strategy only pays if supply can scale with demand; any constraint on capacity turns the commoditization bet into a revenue ceiling.
insights.quote: China’s AI developers are pursuing a low-margin, high-volume business of offering cheap models to a vast number of users

insights.claim: US export controls on advanced chips prevent Chinese AI developers from scaling computing power enough to meet rising demand, and these capacity constraints are currently materially limiting their revenue growth, though they may ease over time as domestic chip production expands.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Chinese AI revenue upside is gated by domestic chip supply; expansion of China's local chip output is the key unlock to monitor for a re-rating.
insights.quote: for now the capacity constraints are materially limiting the revenue growth of China’s AI developers
